verdicts.reading: By 2012 half of traveling workers will travel without a notebook PC, using other devices instead.
verdicts.reason: Edition text now read: the claim is about traveling workers leaving the notebook behind in favour of pocketable devices and web apps. Looked for a 2011-2012 survey of business travelers or mobile workers measuring the share who travel without a notebook. The iPass Mobile Workforce Reports (quarterly, 1,100+ enterprises, 2011-2012) are the closest series; they report devices carried (3.5 devices for work in Q1 2012, 'at least one laptop'), tablet adoption (64%) and desktop abandonment (38%), but never the share leaving the notebook at home on trips. Tablet ownership is a different quantity (D23). No public measure of the stated quantity at 2011-2012.
verdicts.fetched: Gartner 2008 edition press release (Wayback 2008-12-17 capture); iPass Mobile Workforce Report press releases Q2 2011 to Q4 2012 (Wayback); iPass Q4 2012 report (SlideShare).

verdicts.reading: By 2012 high-definition video meeting (telepresence) solutions will replace 2.1 million airline seats a year, costing travel and hospitality US$3.5 billion a year.
verdicts.reason: Edition text now read (Sydney release, 2009-02-06): a modelled displacement of seats by telepresence. Seats displaced by telepresence is an attributed value (D23); IATA, ICAO and airline traffic statistics report passengers carried, not seats substituted by video meetings, and no travel-industry body measured the substitution for 2011-2012. Page access does not change this.

verdicts.reading: By 2014, 90% of organizations will support corporate applications on employee-owned notebooks and smartphones (i.e. allow BYOD for work applications).
verdicts.reason: Edition text says the claim is about supporting corporate applications on employee-owned notebooks and smartphones, which is what organization-level BYOD surveys measure (organization allows employees to use own devices for work). In-window estimates (2013-2014, D23): Tech Pro Research Feb 2013, 44% of organizations allowing BYOD (18% more planning, 37% vetoed); Tech Pro Research Nov 2014, 74% using or planning to allow, about a quarter ruled out, with currently allowed at 71% for firms of 50-249 staff and 54% for the largest firms reported. Even the upper bound (74%, which includes plans) is 21.6% below 90; currently-allowed shares (44-71%) put 90 more than 25% above the actual. Median of in-window estimates is well under 72, so 90 is beyond 25%: miss under D10. Cisco IBSG 89% 'enable BYOD in some form' is from 2012, outside the target-year window, and not used.
verdicts.fetched: Gartner Nov 2010 edition text (Wayback); ZDNet report of Tech Pro Research Nov 2014 and Feb 2013 BYOD surveys (Wayback); PhoneArena summary of the 2014 survey (Wayback). Before, the Tech Pro Research/ZDNet page was not reachable.

verdicts.reading: By 2015 industrialized low-cost cloud services will cannibalize up to 15% of the revenue of the top IT outsourcing providers.
verdicts.reason: Edition text now read: cannibalization of current and potential outsourcing revenue by low-cost cloud services. Revenue lost to cloud substitution is an attributed value (D23); outsourcers' filings report total and segment revenue, not revenue cannibalized by cloud, and no tracker publishes that attribution for 2014-2015. 'Up to' also makes the figure a ceiling. No public measure.
